To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the herd protection of an oral cholera vaccination campaign in Bangladesh could be unmasked by reanalyzing the cluster-randomized effectiveness data to include only innermost households in the clusters.

the effectiveness of an oral cholera vaccination programme in reducing cholera cases in a densely populated area was 46%, that the effectiveness of the vaccination programme in reducing cases in people who were not vaccinated was 16% and that the effectiveness of vaccination in reducing cases in the population was 58%.

in a densely populated, urban setting, oral cholera vaccine (OCV) herd protection was masked in the original cluster-randomized trial (CRT) analysis, but was detected by analysing the innermost 75%, 50%, and 25% households of the OCV clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new vaccine against cholera, the causative agent of cholera, and the development of new ways to deliver vaccines.
the development of a new generation of vaccines against cholera, which is caused by Vibrio cholerae.
the development of a novel, non-invasive diagnostic test for Chlamydia trachomatis (C. trachomatis), which is the causative agent of trachoma, the leading cause of preventable blindness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OCVs confer both direct protection and substantial herd protection, but that these effects may vary by population setting.
herd immunity was demonstrated for the innermost households in this cluster-randomized trial.
the OCV herd protection effect was masked in our original analyses of all cluster residents and was only unmasked in the innermost subclusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the vaccine was highly effective, but that the effect was attenuated by the high level of cholera transmission in the community.
the herd protection by OCVs in a densely populated setting is substantial and that the analysis of innermost households of clusters may help to unmask herd effects in cluster trials.
OCVs can be used to control cholera epidemics and can be used to protect the population in endemic areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the definition of the cluster is very important.
the herd effects from the oral cholera vaccine were masked by the fact that we had not accounted for the spatial distribution of the cholera cases.
the herd protection conferred by OCVs is substantial, and that it can be masked in cluster randomized trials if the clusters are defined to include areas where the vaccine does not reach.
